questions.question: What does MVC stand for in software design and Human-Computer Interaction?
What design pattern in HCI and software design divides a system into three distinct parts: Model, View, and Controller?
What is the primary purpose of the Model-View-Controller (MVC) design pattern?
questions.answer: To make programs easier to build, understand, and fix

questions.question: Which component of MVC is described as 'the brain' of the system, handling data and logic?
Which component of MVC is described as 'the face' of the system, representing what the user sees?
Which component of MVC is described as 'the hands' of the system, representing what the user does?
In the restaurant analogy for MVC, what corresponds to the kitchen where food is prepared?
In the restaurant analogy for MVC, what corresponds to the menu and food served that the customer sees?
In the restaurant analogy for MVC, what corresponds to the waiter who takes the order and delivers it between the kitchen and the customer?
Which component stores and manages the system’s data and rules?
Which component knows everything about the system’s content?
What component updates data when something changes and does not care about how things look on screen?
Without which component would the program have no knowledge to show?
What is defined as the visual representation of the data in the MVC design pattern?
Which MVC component shows information to the user in a friendly way and changes automatically when the Model updates?
Without which component can users not see or interact with the data?
Which component acts as a bridge between the user and the system?
Which MVC component takes input from the user, decides what action to perform, and tells the Model or View what to do?
Without which component can the user not communicate with the system?
In the MVC flow, which component handles the initial action when a user clicks, taps, or types?
In the MVC flow, after receiving input, what component does the Controller update?
In the MVC flow, after data is updated, what component does the Model notify of changes?
In the human body analogy for MVC, what represents the Model?
In the human body analogy for MVC, what represents the Controller?
In the human body analogy for MVC, what represents the View?
In the music app analogy for MVC, what represents the Model?
In the music app analogy for MVC, what represents the View?
In the music app analogy for MVC, what represents the Controller?
Which benefit of MVC ensures that designers can work on the View while programmers work on the Model?
Which benefit of MVC allows one Model to work with different Views?
Which benefit of MVC ensures that changes in one part do not break the others?
Which benefit of MVC describes each part having its own job?
Enumerate the three main components of the Model-View-Controller (MVC) design pattern.
Enumerate the informal descriptions/metaphors given for the three parts of MVC (e.g., 'the brain').
Enumerate the three components in the restaurant analogy for MVC.
Enumerate the functions of the Model in the MVC pattern.
answers: Knows everything about the system’s content.
Does not care about how things look on screen.

questions.question: Enumerate the functions of the View in the MVC pattern.
answers: Shows information to the user in a friendly way.
Changes automatically when the Model updates.

questions.question: Enumerate the functions of the Controller in the MVC pattern.
answers: Takes input from the user (clicks, taps, voice, typing).
Tells the Model or View what to do.

questions.question: Enumerate examples of user inputs handled by the Controller.
Enumerate in sequence the 4 steps of how MVC works together (the interaction flow).
answers: 1. User does something (click, tap, type) -> handled by Controller.
3. Model notifies the View of changes.
4. View shows the updated information to the User.

questions.question: Enumerate the four main benefits of using the MVC design pattern.
Enumerate the three elements of the Human body analogy recap for MVC.
Enumerate the three elements of the Music app analogy recap for MVC.
Enumerate what missing each of the three MVC components results in for the system.
answers: Without the Model: program has no knowledge to show.
Without the View: users can’t see or interact with the data.
Without the Controller: user cannot communicate with the system.

Enumerate the three analogies used to explain MVC in Chapter 6.

answers: To make programs easier to build
